description.en: The DOI System provides persistent, resolvable identifiers for digital objects, managed by registration agencies such as DataCite and Crossref.
A general-purpose distributed system for assigning, managing and resolving persistent identifiers; the underlying technology for DOIs.
A redirection service, now operated by the Internet Archive, providing stable URLs that can be repointed as resource locations change.
A permanent URL redirection service for Linked Data and Semantic Web vocabularies, maintained by the W3C Permanent Identifier Community Group.
A persistent identifier scheme designed to support long-term access to information objects, widely used by libraries and archives.
Provides a persistent, unique identifier for researchers to distinguish themselves and connect their research contributions.
A global, community-led registry providing persistent identifiers for research organizations.
A general-purpose metadata vocabulary of properties and classes for describing resources, maintained by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative.
A W3C RDF vocabulary for describing data catalogs, datasets, distributions and services to enable interoperable data discovery.
A collaborative, cross-vendor vocabulary for structured data markup on web pages, widely used to describe datasets via schema:Dataset.
A list of core metadata properties for accurate and consistent identification of research data and other outputs for citation and discovery.
Defines the schema for describing geographic information and services, including identification, extent, quality and distribution metadata.
An international standard for describing data from the social, behavioral and economic sciences across the research data lifecycle.
A biodiversity data standard providing a stable, extensible vocabulary of terms for sharing information about biological diversity.

label.en: MIAME (Minimum Information About a Microarray Experiment)

description.en: Specifies the minimum information required to unambiguously interpret and independently verify microarray experiment results.
The CEDAR Workbench lets researchers author, share and reuse metadata templates to produce structured, standards-compliant metadata.
A machine-actionable data management plan (maDMP) schema enabling DMPs to be exchanged and processed automatically by tools and systems.
Adds typed HTTP Link headers and link relations that make the relationship between a resource, its metadata and related resources machine-discoverable.
A lightweight method to package research data together with machine-readable JSON-LD metadata describing the data, its context and provenance.
The dcat:Distribution class links a dataset's metadata record to its actual accessible data files, formats and access URLs.
A discovery service for exploring connections between research outputs, people, organizations and funders using DataCite and ORCID metadata.
A search engine for discovering datasets indexed from their schema.org and DCAT metadata across the web.
A global registry of research data repositories covering a wide range of academic disciplines.
A curated, searchable registry of standards, databases and data policies across scientific disciplines.
A EUDAT metadata catalogue that harvests and indexes research data from EUDAT and other repositories for cross-disciplinary discovery.
An open discovery portal for publications, datasets, software and other research products linked across European infrastructures.
A general-purpose open repository operated by CERN that lets researchers deposit and discover datasets, software and publications.
An open-source repository platform for sharing, citing and preserving research data, deployed by institutions worldwide.
An open-source repository software platform used by institutions to manage and provide searchable access to digital collections.
HTTP layered over TLS encryption; the standard secure protocol for transferring data and metadata over the Web.
The Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting provides an application-independent framework for harvesting metadata between repositories.
Defines how SPARQL queries and updates are transmitted to a SPARQL processing service over HTTP.
FTP and its secure variant SFTP are standard protocols for transferring files between a client and a server over a network.
An authorization framework enabling applications to obtain limited access to a user's resources without exposing their credentials.
An identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0 that lets clients verify user identity and obtain basic profile information.
An XML-based OASIS standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity and service providers.
An international interfederation service that interconnects research and education identity federations for federated access.
An open-source federated identity and access management system implementing SAML-based single sign-on for web applications.
Lets researchers authenticate to third-party systems using their ORCID iD via OAuth 2.0, linking actions to their persistent identifier.
A community-based certification for trustworthy data repositories, assessing their policies for long-term data and metadata preservation.
Harvard Dataverse's published policy describing how deposited data and metadata are curated and preserved for the long term.
Zenodo's general policies, including its commitment to preserve deposited content and metadata for the lifetime of the CERN data centre.
The W3C data model and abstract syntax for representing information as subject-predicate-object triples on the Web.
The W3C Web Ontology Language for representing rich, machine-interpretable knowledge via classes, properties and axioms.
The Simple Knowledge Organization System, a W3C model for expressing controlled vocabularies, thesauri and taxonomies as machine-readable RDF.
A W3C standard for expressing Linked Data using JSON syntax, allowing data to carry semantic context.
A vocabulary for annotating and validating the structure, content and semantics of JSON documents.
Defines the structure, content and semantics of XML documents through a machine-processable schema language.
The Shapes Constraint Language, a W3C language for validating RDF graphs against a set of conditions expressed as shapes.
The U.S. National Library of Medicine's controlled vocabulary thesaurus used for indexing biomedical literature.
The World Health Organization's international classification of diseases and related health conditions.
A comprehensive, multilingual clinical healthcare terminology used for recording and exchanging clinical data.
FAO's multilingual controlled vocabulary covering agriculture, forestry, fisheries, food and related domains.
The GEneral Multilingual Environmental Thesaurus, a controlled vocabulary of environmental terminology maintained by the European Environment Agency.
Integrates and distributes key biomedical terminologies and standards to enable interoperability among health information systems.
A crowd-sourced community effort providing a structured, Linked Data knowledge graph extracted from Wikipedia.
A free, collaborative knowledge base providing structured Linked Data usable across the Wikimedia projects and beyond.
An RDF vocabulary and ontology for describing people, their attributes and their social connections.
A public domain dedication that waives all copyright and related rights to a work, allowing unrestricted reuse.
Permits unrestricted reuse and redistribution of a work provided that appropriate credit is given to the creator.
Permits reuse and adaptation with attribution, provided derivative works are shared under the same licence.
Permits reuse and adaptation with attribution for non-commercial purposes only.
Allows free reuse of a database provided that attribution is given to its creator.
A share-alike licence for databases requiring attribution and that derivative databases remain open.
A short, permissive software licence allowing reuse with minimal restrictions, requiring only preservation of the copyright notice.
A permissive licence that additionally grants an express patent licence from contributors to users.
The W3C OWL ontology for representing and interchanging provenance information generated in different systems and contexts.
The W3C conceptual data model for provenance, defining the core entities, activities and agents used to describe a resource's history.
An earlier community model and interchange format for representing the provenance of process and data, precursor to PROV.
